cells.tense: You're in the middle of it now, and the clearing is coming from something you actually understood — you're deciding what goes, and you're right about it.
cells.ask: Give the steady hour to the thing you're building, in your own company, and let it bring you closer to people rather than further from them.
cells.core:
This is what it looks like when the choosing is working: you can name which arrangement is held up by habit alone, you say so, and the saying lands. What falls, falls cleanly. Nothing dramatic about it — just more room in the day than there was this morning, and you're the one who made it. There's a steadiness under the whole thing. You're not waiting for permission and you're not performing the choice for anyone. It's simply yours, and it holds.

What's left needs the quieter work now: the same small practice, kept up on ordinary days. That isn't less than the clearing. It's the part that makes the clearing last — the hours nobody sees, the thing you keep refining because you want it true. That's what this open ground is free to feed next.
cells.sheetLine: You cleared what couldn't stand, you know why, and you're choosing what stays.

cells.tense: You're already bracing for the next thing to come down, and you're knocking at walls that are still holding — ahead of anything that's actually asking to fall.
cells.ask: Say one thing out loud to someone who's been carrying this with you, and let their version of it change yours.
cells.core:
At its best, this is a person who can walk into a room and tell, plainly, which of the structures is hollow — and then take it apart with almost no fuss, because the truth was already doing the work. That's a real gift, and people trust it. They bring you the knot and you find the one thread that undoes it.

Right now the tearing-down has its own momentum. You can't let anything stand long enough to find out whether it would have — and every collapse you didn't need teaches the people around you to hold their cards closer. What settles that isn't another demolition. It's putting one piece of what you've found in front of someone else and letting it live between you, where it can be argued with and handed on.
cells.sheetLine: Everything looks like it should come down, and you're not letting anything stand long enough to tell.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that's already behind you, holding up something you already know stopped holding — and you're still calling it standing.
cells.ask: Build one small structure this week — a fixed time, a fixed way of doing it — and let it hold something you actually care about.
cells.core:
When this is working, you're the one who reads the room before anyone else does: you notice that the schedule no longer fits the work, that the arrangement has stopped matching what it was made for — and you act on it while it's still small. That reading is reliable. People count on it. It's why the collapses you call happen late and gently instead of all at once.

It isn't showing up right now. You're propping up something that already came loose, telling yourself it's still load-bearing, and the strength that would go into the next clear look is going into the prop. Don't try to feel your way out. Make one plain thing instead — a time, a shape, a way of doing it you can repeat. Structure that serves what it holds does the choosing for you, and the direction comes back with it.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding up something that already fell, and calling it holding.

cells.tense: You're already choosing — the next move has been happening through you for a while — and you're talking about it as though it were still up in the air.
cells.ask: Follow the one thing you actually want into today's action, on the pull alone, and skip the case you'd have to make for it.
cells.core:
This is what it looks like when it's clean: you want something, you say which, and your days arrange themselves around the saying. There's no ceremony to it. Someone asks what you're doing next and you can answer in a sentence, and the answer is true — that's the whole capacity, direction that doesn't need defending because it's already yours.

Something is coming down around you. You've felt the ground move for a while — you know which of your arrangements has already gone loose — and you keep describing it as completely open, as if the decision were still ahead of you instead of already underway through your hands. Go down one level. Not the argument for the change — the plain wanting under it. Move on the thing you'd move on if nobody were watching you make the case.
